title: So Deep That: Results in Roads and Ports

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *tan … que*, *tanto … que* and *de tal manera que* from B2 Unit 31. They say how much of something led to a real result, so the verb after *que* is in the indicative. Roads, passes and ports give plenty of cases: how deep, how snowy, how high.

items.spanish: El puerto de Chancay es tan profundo que recibe barcos muy grandes.
items.english: The port of Chancay is so deep that it receives very large ships.

items.spanish: Nieva tanto en la cordillera que, a veces, el paso de Los Libertadores se cierra.
items.english: It snows so much in the mountains that sometimes the Los Libertadores pass closes.

items.spanish: Los Andes son tan altos que durante siglos separaron la costa del Pacífico del interior.
items.english: The Andes are so high that for centuries they separated the Pacific coast from the interior.

items.spanish: La carretera Interoceánica une Brasil y Perú de tal manera que los camiones cruzan los Andes.
items.english: The Interoceanic Highway joins Brazil and Peru in such a way that lorries cross the Andes.

sections.content: *Tan* goes before an adjective or an adverb and never changes. After a verb, or before a noun, use *tanto* (*tantos camiones*). The result is real, so the verb after *que* is in the indicative.
